<!-- docs/compatibility.md -->

# Compatibility

The **supported bands are exactly the CI-tested matrix**: the
`compat` workflow proves `{floor, latest-in-band}` for every band
below (each Payload line, Better Auth, Auth.js, both Next majors,
TanStack Start and Router) on Node 20, 22, and 24 wherever the
upstream's own `engines` allow (build + unit + schema-probe), the e2e
suites run every release against SQLite (Chromium, Firefox, and
WebKit), Postgres, and mongo (Chromium), and the golden-DB tests keep the
previous minor's database booting. A range below is a promise only
as wide as those cells; the runtime version assertions
(`UnsupportedVersionError` at wiring time) enforce the same bands
before any database write.

Support policy: recommend **exact pins** for upstreams in your
lockfile (the manifests' ranges exist so fresh installs resolve
something tested, not so every version is blessed). After an
upstream minor lands, the compat patch that widens the band is the
next release — file or watch an issue; until then the old band
holds and the assertion fails fast with a typed error instead of
letting an unvalidated version touch your database.

**Better Auth lockstep (three-way rule):** `better-auth` core and
every `@better-auth/*` satellite you enable (`@better-auth/passkey`
today) move **together**, and only within our validated band.
Satellites peer-lock to exact BA minors — when a satellite ships for
BA 1.8, installing it forces BA 1.8 under you — so bump satellites
and core in one commit, run the provider's schema probe (it fails
fast on unvalidated BA schemas), and never let a satellite drag you
outside the band: the version assertion will refuse to boot, which
is the intended outcome. Probed satellites: `@better-auth/passkey`
and `@better-auth/api-key` (both in the committed schema probe and
the compat matrix). Unprobed: `@better-auth/sso` is **unsupported
until probed** — adding it meets `UnsupportedSchemaError` with this
same fail-fast.

## Runtimes and frameworks

| Dependency                               | Validated (floor / installed) | Range (peer unless noted)           | Notes                                                                               |
| ---------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | ----------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `payload`                                | 3.83.0 / 3.91.0               | `^3.83.0 \|\| 4.0.0-beta.0`         | v3 for Next; 3.83 is the named-plugin/global-hook floor; v4 pin is exact            |
| `payload` (Start)                        | 4.0.0-beta.0                  | exact beta pin (example)            | `@payloadcms/tanstack-start` exists only on the v4 line                             |
| `better-auth`                            | 1.7.6 / 1.7.7                 | `>=1.7.6 <1.8.0`                    | Type-level floor 1.7.6 (`modelKey` types); validated 1.7 line only — lockstep above |
| `@auth/core`                             | 0.41.0 / 0.41.3               | `>=0.41.0 <0.42.0`                  | Raw core, not the `next-auth` wrapper; 0.x minors add Adapter methods               |
| `next`                                   | 15.0.0 / 16.4.0               | `^15.0.0 \|\| ^16.0.0` (next pkg)   | Both majors typecheck; 16.4 e2e-tested by the example                               |
| `@tanstack/react-start` / `react-router` | 1.140.2 / 1.168.61 · 1.170.41 | `^1.140.2` / `^1.170.0` (start pkg) | 1.140.2 is the `createMiddleware` types floor                                       |
| `vite` (Start)                           | 8.3.4                         | dev (example)                       | + `@vitejs/plugin-rsc`, `react-server-dom-webpack` for Payload admin                |
| `react` / `react-dom`                    | 19.2.6                        | `^19.0.0` (peer, UI pkgs)           |                                                                                     |
| `neverthrow`                             | 8.2.0                         | dep                                 | `Result`/`ResultAsync` throughout                                                   |
| `zod`                                    | 4.6.5 (floor 4.0.0)           | dep                                 | Boundary schemas + branded types; floor proven by probe (see below)                 |
| `@standard-schema/spec`                  | 1.1.0                         | dep (types)                         | Every exported schema is a Standard Schema v1                                       |
| `typescript` (consumer)                  | 5.5.4 / 6.0.3                 | —                                   | Floor is 5.5; 5.0 fails inside Zod 4.6's own types (`NoInfer`)                      |
| `effect`                                 | 3.22.2                        | dev only                            | Interop tested in CI; never a runtime dependency (recipe below)                     |
| `bun`                                    | 1.4.2                         | `packageManager`                    | CI pins the same                                                                    |
| `node`                                   | 20.9+ / 22                    | `engines`                           | All packages ESM-only (`type: module`)                                              |

Module resolution: shipped code builds under `nodenext`, except
`@payload-auth-link/next`, which uses `esnext`/`bundler` because
Next.js ships no `exports` map for `next/*` subpaths. Tests run
under bundler resolution for the same reason.

Payload v4 (4.0.0-beta.0): the plugin's whole test suite runs on it in
the compat matrix (`payload-4-beta`). Two v4 changes matter to host
code next to the plugin: the Local API now defaults to
`overrideAccess: false` (every plugin call sets it explicitly; your own
setup scripts may need `overrideAccess: true`), and `createdBy` /
`updatedBy` are filled from `req.user`, whose `id` the plugin keeps in
the database's own type (a number on SQLite/Postgres).

Payload 3.83.0 and 3.84.0 (the band floor) do not pass `req` to auth
strategies, so the strategy cannot share its session resolution with
the plugin's endpoint through `req.context`: a refused request logs
"no provider session resolved" twice there. From 3.84.1 it is logged
once. Behaviour and security are otherwise identical.

## Databases

| Adapter                   | Validated how                                                                         |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `@payloadcms/db-sqlite`   | Unit integration (in-memory) + `bun run e2e`                                          |
| `@payloadcms/db-postgres` | `bun run e2e:postgres` (per-run database, `push: true`), GH service in CI             |
| `@payloadcms/db-mongodb`  | `bun run e2e:mongo` (per-run wiredTiger memory replset, transactions off — see below) |

Product code issues only single-document Local API calls, so the
parity risk sits in Where translation, date serialization, and id
types — all six suites assert identical behavior (33 specs each:
`e2e`, `e2e:postgres`, `e2e:mongo` on Next; `e2e:tanstack`,
`e2e:tanstack-postgres`, `e2e:tanstack-mongo` on Start). Each
example's mongo branch disables Payload transactions: several
Payload instances (plugin + provider loaders) lock-fight on a
single-node memory server. Production mongo deployments keep
transactions on; nothing we ship depends on their absence.

## Browsers

The SQLite suites (`e2e`, `e2e:tanstack`) run in Chromium, Firefox,
and WebKit (Playwright Desktop Chrome / Firefox / Safari profiles),
one engine after another against the same server. Postgres and Mongo
suites run Chromium only. Traces are kept on failure; CI retries
exist as a backstop, but specs pass with retries off. The shipped UI
is unstyled primitives with no browser-specific APIs beyond `fetch`
and `location`.

## Sign-in capabilities by provider

Canonical capability matrix (how to wire each row:
[Capabilities guide](guide-capabilities.md)). Capabilities are
**declared per provider and checked at wiring** — configuring a
feature on an undeclared capability throws
`UnsupportedCapabilityError` at startup, never silently at runtime.
✅ works · ◐ partial/recipe · — not available.

| Capability                      | Better Auth 1.7.7                    | Auth.js (`@auth/core` 0.41.3) | Notes                                                          |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Email/password                  | ✅                                   | ✅ credentials service        | Verified-email linking gate on both                            |
| Magic link                      | ✅ `magicLink`                       | ✅ Email provider             | Single-use; dev mailbox in examples                            |
| Email OTP                       | ✅ `emailOTP` (native 3-attempt cap) | ✅ recipe helpers             | Auth.js attempts capped by your route                          |
| OAuth / OIDC                    | ✅ social + `genericOAuth`           | ✅ providers                  | Unverified assertions refused; Auth.js needs the D6 allow-list |
| One Tap                         | ✅ `oneTap` plugin                   | ◐ JWKS-verifier recipe        | No live-Google automated proof                                 |
| Passkeys                        | ✅ `@better-auth/passkey`            | — (experimental upstream)     | Session `methods` stay `unknown` (BA marks none)               |
| Two-factor (TOTP)               | ✅ `twoFactor` (enrollment-mapped)   | —                             | `requireMfaForRoles` throws on Auth.js                         |
| Suspend + revoke                | ✅                                   | ✅ database strategy only     | Payload verify gate also covers JWTs                           |
| Impersonation                   | ✅ audited, TTL-bounded              | —                             | Deny layers + audit trail in the plugin                        |
| Phone sign-in                   | ✅ `phoneNumber`                     | —                             | Links existing users only; never provisions                    |
| Anonymous / guest               | ✅ `anonymous`                       | —                             | Guest principal, no Payload access                             |
| Multi-session / bearer / device | ◐ logout sweeps all device sessions  | ◐                             | Admission is explicit (`admitChannels`)                        |
| Organizations                   | ✅ Payload-owned                     | ✅ Payload-owned              | Provider org stores are never authorization                    |
| Enterprise SSO domains          | ◐ registered-provider gate           | ◐ registered-provider gate    | Exact verified-domain match required                           |
| Identity lifecycle events       | ✅                                   | ✅ engine callbacks           | Optional subscription; core works without                      |

Framework support is uniform across the matrix: every row behaves
the same on Next.js and TanStack Start (one framework-free web
core), and every e2e spec runs against both examples.

## Type surface

`attw --profile esm-only` + `publint` gate every package
(`bun run release:check`). Legacy node10/CJS resolution is the
documented non-goal: ESM-only by decision.

More alarms run in `bun run check` so breakage is caught here, not
in your build:

- **API snapshots** (`snapshots/api/*.txt`, `bun run api:check`):
  the full shipped `.d.ts` surface of every package. Any change
  requires a changeset at the right semver level.
- **Schema snapshots** (`snapshots/schema/*.json`,
  `bun run schema:check`): the DB-facing collection shapes both
  providers ship and the plugin's injected users fields. A change
  must carry an `Upgrade impact:` changeset section and a
  [upgrading.md](upgrading.md) entry, or CI fails — a silent shape
  change is a broken user database.
- **Consumer fixture** (`bun run consumer:check`): the built `dist`
  types typechecked with `skipLibCheck: false` under the strictest
  flags, the way a strict consumer compiles.
- **Type pins** (`expectTypeOf` in `type-alarms.test.ts` and the
  adapter inventory alarms in both providers): union inventories,
  schema↔domain-type pairs, and the full `Adapter`/`CustomAdapter`
  method surfaces pinned literal-for-literal — an upstream-added
  adapter method fails `tsc`, not a production request.
- **Payload import inventory** (`payload-inventory.test.ts`): every
  `payload`/`payload/shared` symbol shipped source imports is
  pinned; a new import (which sets the real Payload floor) fails CI
  until it is verified against the band and noted here.
  `CollectionBeforeDeleteHook` (organization delete cascade and the
  last-owner guard) and `CollectionAfterDeleteHook` (the last-owner
  guard's post-write re-check) are type-only imports present across
  the whole Payload 3 band and v4. The guard also calls
  `payload.db.updateOne` and `payload.db.create` (the database
  adapter contract, present on every adapter in the band) to lock
  the organization row and to restore a refused removal.
  `CollectionAfterReadHook` (the authentication-time credential gate,
  GHSA-mjvh) is a type-only import present across the whole band. The
  gate relies on Payload's local-JWT and API-key strategies loading the
  user through the users collection's Local API with the request's
  `req` and `overrideAccess` (`findByID` / `find` on `apiKeyIndex`),
  which holds on 3.83+ and 4.0.0-beta.0;
  `integration-local-credential-gate.test.ts` fails if a release stops
  doing so.

## Schema interoperability (Zod, Effect, Standard Schema)

Core's boundary schemas (`emailSchema`, `roleSchema`,
`providerIdSchema`, `phoneNumberSchema`, `linkingPolicySchema`,
`collectionMapSchema`, `startupConfigSchema`) are Zod 4 schemas and
therefore Standard Schema v1 objects: each carries
`~standard.validate` with `StandardSchemaV1.InferOutput` equal to
its domain type (`Email`, `Role`, …). That is the supported
composition surface for every schema ecosystem:

- **Do not** nest an exported schema inside a Zod 3 schema; the
  majors are runtime-incompatible. Compose through `~standard`, or
  validate with the paired parser (`parseEmail`, `parseRole`, …)
  and keep the branded result.
- **Effect users:** decode through `~standard.validate` inside
  `Effect.tryPromise`, convert your own schemas with
  `Schema.standardSchemaV1`, and lift neverthrow `ResultAsync` port
  calls with `Effect.promise` + `Result.match` (they never reject
  by contract). The recipe is pinned by
  `packages/core/src/__tests__/effect-interop.test.ts`, which runs
  in CI against the current Effect release; `effect` stays a
  devDependency — nothing shipped imports it.
- The `zod: ^4.0.0` floor is proven, not assumed: core source
  typechecks against Zod 4.0.0 and the built package passes a
  runtime probe on 4.0.0 (Better Auth's own `^4.5.4` requirement
  will float most real trees higher).

## payload-auth parity (migration, issues #49–#59)

An app coming from [`payload-auth`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/payload-auth)
(the Better Auth-as-Payload-users plugin) maps onto this package
feature by feature. Each row names the payload-auth feature, its
payload-auth-link equivalent, and the support status; migration
issues are linked where they close a gap. The contract behind every
"adopt/import" claim is the **payload-auth fixture database** — a real
dump produced by running payload-auth 1.9.4 itself
(`fixtures/dumps/`, `fixtures/payload-auth-app/`), loaded by the
`migration-fixture` CI job. The public
[migrating-from-payload-auth guide](migrating-from-payload-auth.md)
is generated from these artifacts, never maintained by hand.

| payload-auth feature                                    | payload-auth-link equivalent                                                                    | Status                          | Notes & issues                                                                          |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Email+password sign-in                                  | `createBetterAuthEngine` with `emailAndPassword`                                                | full                            | Same Better Auth engine; hashes are portable (fixture pins the hash shape)              |
| Email verification                                      | Engine default `requireEmailVerification: true`                                                 | full (stricter default)         | 0.7.0 requires opt-out; payload-auth defaulted off                                      |
| Social OAuth sign-in                                    | `socialProviders` through the engine                                                            | full                            |                                                                                         |
| Magic link / email OTP / anonymous / passkey            | The same Better Auth plugins, `autoDeclare`d                                                    | full                            | passkey probed (`@better-auth/passkey`)                                                 |
| Two-factor                                              | BA `twoFactor` plugin + `policies.requireMfaForRoles` projection                                | partial                         | MFA assurance is capability-gated (see the capabilities guide); admin step-up view: #55 |
| Organization plugin (orgs/members/invites)              | BA organization plugin via `autoDeclare`/`customModels`; payload-auth-link adds role governance | partial → full with #49         | Adopt the app's business collections without row moves (#49)                            |
| Users collection IS the BA user table                   | Separate link: identities live in plugin-injected fields on the users document                  | via #49 (adopt) or #50 (import) | Zero row moves with `schemaMap` (#49); reversible copy otherwise (#50)                  |
| API keys (`@better-auth/api-key`)                       | Engine `autoDeclare` + Payload REST authentication by key                                       | full                            | Probed satellite; key→session bridge becomes `authLinkServer` (#54)                     |
| `jwt` plugin + `jwks`                                   | Engine `autoDeclare` of the `jwks` model                                                        | full                            | Carried verbatim by the importer (#50)                                                  |
| OIDC provider (`oidcProvider`)                          | Removed upstream in BA 1.7 → `@better-auth/oauth-provider`                                      | gap (app-side schema move)      | Journey issue #60 documents the 1:1 data map                                            |
| `@better-auth/sso`, device authorization, subscriptions | Not probed — the engine fails fast with `UnsupportedSchemaError`                                | unsupported until probed        | See the Better Auth lockstep rule above                                                 |
| Admin login/signup views                                | `admin: { loginView: 'provider' }` views                                                        | gap → #55                       | Since 0.7.0 linked documents refuse Payload local login by design                       |
| Admin forgot/reset views                                | Provider-flow forgot/reset views                                                                | gap → #55                       | Provider-linked documents refuse the Payload reset flow (GHSA-f4hj)                     |
| Admin invitations (`admin-invitations`)                 | Role-manager governance (create operator accounts, invite to roles)                             | partial                         | payload-auth's admin-invite collection is superseded by role governance                 |
| `defaultAdminRole` / `adminRoles`                       | `roles` + `roleManagerRoles` plugin options                                                     | full                            |                                                                                         |
| `requireAdminInviteForSignUp`                           | `policies` + JIT-link rules (verified-email gate)                                               | partial                         | Sign-up surface is the provider's; unverified emails never link                         |
| `getPayloadAuth(config)`                                | `getPayload({ config })`                                                                        | codemod → #53                   |                                                                                         |
| `payload.betterAuth.api.*`                              | `authLinkServer(payload)` supported session API; opt-in shim meanwhile                          | shim → #53, API → #54           | The shim goes through the same suspension/MFA gate — no back door                       |
| `payload.betterAuth.handler`                            | `auth.handler` via the framework adapter (`createRouteHandlers`)                                | full                            |                                                                                         |
| Admin views (user/account/session lists)                | Payload admin on the users collection + `ba-*`/adopted collections                              | full with #49                   | Adopted collections keep their admin config (#49)                                       |
| `saveToJWT` field flags                                 | Payload-native (Payload owns the session JWT)                                                   | full                            |                                                                                         |
| `hidePluginCollections`                                 | `collectionsAccess` (default deny-all) + hidden admin on engine collections                     | full                            |                                                                                         |
| Role values like `frontPlugin` (stored as-is)           | `roleValues` map at the storage edge + `projectRolesAs`                                         | full                            | No `ALTER TYPE` rename required; proven on the fixture                                  |
| Full user document on `req.user`                        | `reqUser: 'document'` (opt-in; projection by default)                                           | gap → #57                       |                                                                                         |
| Legacy session cookies at cutover                       | `legacySessions: { until }` read-only coexistence window                                        | gap → #51                       | Cookie names exposed through the cookie helpers                                         |
| Uninstall / off-ramp                                    | Tested uninstall job + `migrate export`                                                         | gap → #58                       |                                                                                         |
| Session carry across cutover                            | Importer `--sessions=carry` (default) + coexistence window                                      | gap → #50/#51                   |                                                                                         |

Rows move to **full** only when the fixture CI job proves them: the
fixture boots (#49), old passwords sign in (#50), legacy cookies hold
across the switch (#51), and the doctor's report matches the known
blocker list (#52).

<!-- docs/troubleshooting.md -->

# Troubleshooting

Every entry below is a failure mode hit while building this project,
with the fix that resolved it. Symptoms first.

## Everyone bounces to sign-in (including fresh logins)

The middleware's cookie names don't match the engine's. The names in
`lib/auth-cookie-names.ts` must mirror the engine options exactly —
custom `advanced.cookies` names (Better Auth) or
`cookies.sessionToken.name` (Auth.js) included. A mismatch fails closed by design. Compare the
`set-cookie` response headers against your names list.

## Auth.js sign-in shows the form error, or lands on the Auth.js error page

The credentials callback always 302s; read the final URL (see the
[Auth.js guide](guide-authjs.md)). If _every_ login fails, check the
server log for `CredentialsSignin` (wrong password / unknown user —
expected for bad credentials) versus `Configuration` (missing
secret, untrusted host). If the user exists but login never sticks,
the row is unverified — the plugin links verified identities only.

## `UnsupportedStrategy` 500s on every Auth.js action

Credentials + database session strategy. Auth.js rejects that
combination at config time; the engine fail-fasts first — including
through factory-wrapped providers, which it inspects by calling them
with `{}` exactly as Auth.js does
(`packages/provider-authjs/src/engine.ts`, covered by the engine
suite's factory tests). A credentials provider in any form without
explicit `session: { strategy: 'jwt' }` throws at wiring with the fix
attached; a factory that throws on inspection fails at wiring as
`provider factory threw` (Auth.js would throw identically on first
request — the factory must tolerate `{}`).

So a request-time 500 means a genuine problem, not an inspection
miss: either the served config really lacks the jwt strategy (check
that the route serves the engine's `config` — a hand-composed `Auth()`
bypasses the fail-fast), or a factory threw (read the wiring error,
not the 500 page). Fix: `Credentials(...)` — direct or via a
`{}`-tolerant factory — with explicit `session: { strategy: 'jwt' }`.

## `AdapterMappingError` / `UnsupportedSchemaError` on login

A storage row is corrupt (missing id field, wrong date shape, account
without `userId`). Auth.js throws `AdapterMappingError` naming the
field — inspect the `aj-*` row directly. Better Auth's equivalent
fail-fast is `UnsupportedSchemaError` on the `ba-*` row. Fix or
delete the row; this never becomes a silent login failure — that is
the point.

The same error at **boot** (not login) usually means a Better Auth
plugin contributes a field or model this adapter has not declared.
Satellites probed by the committed schema probe (declare their models
in `customModels` exactly as the probe does, and they work):
`@better-auth/passkey` and `@better-auth/api-key` (verified end to end
— see the [API keys recipe](guide-capabilities.md#api-keys)). Still
unprobed: `@better-auth/sso` — composing it fails fast with
`UnsupportedSchemaError` until support lands. Every plugin exported
by `better-auth/plugins` is covered by the probe.

## `SQLITE_ERROR: no such column: …` (or `42703` on Postgres) at boot or on first use

The code is newer than the database: a column this version selects
or writes does not exist in your tables. This is the raw shape of an
**unmigrated upgrade** (B1) — the 0.1.1 → 0.2.0 move added
`aj-verification-tokens.key` and the `users` governance fields, and
booting 0.2.x on an unmigrated 0.1.1 database died exactly this way
on the first `users` query.

Map the missing column to the fix:

- `users.phone` / `users.suspendedUntil` / `users.suspendReason` →
  0.1.1 → 0.2.x upgrade steps in
  [upgrading.md](upgrading.md#011--020): boot once with push on
  (dev), or generate/apply the migration (production). All three
  columns are optional; no backfill needed.
- `aj_verification_tokens.key` → same section. After a 0.2.1+ boot
  the column exists nullable; if your database instead shows the
  old table recreation damage (empty `aj-verification-tokens`,
  half-migrated `ba_users` on SQLite), that was 0.2.0-exact with
  push on — restore from backup or re-create the token rows, then
  upgrade to 0.2.1+.
- On MongoDB you will never see this error — drift surfaces as
  silently wrong indexes instead. If you upgraded the Auth.js
  provider and the composite-token behavior seems absent, run
  `reconcileAuthJsMongoIndexes(payload)` (see the 0.1.1 → 0.2.0
  section).
- Column exists but a `NOT NULL` insert fails (`key`) → an old
  0.2.0 migration made it required; drop and re-add it nullable per
  the upgrading.md SQL sketch.

Prevention: upgrade through one version heading at a time, keep
`bun run schema:check`-style migration review in your deploy, and
check `docs/upgrading.md` for the version you are adopting before
bumping. The runtime `UnsupportedVersionError` catches upstream
version drift at boot; missing columns mean the **database** half
of an upgrade was skipped.

## `UnsupportedVersionError` at boot

An upstream (`payload`, `better-auth`, `@auth/core`) sits outside
the validated band — found vs supported are both in the message.
Pin the named package back inside the band (exact versions in
[compatibility.md](compatibility.md)) and wait for the compat patch
that widens it. The refusal happens before any database write by
design: an unvalidated upstream must not touch your data.

## Edge build fails importing `payload` / database code

Something in `middleware.ts`'s import graph reaches the engine or
`payload.config`. Middleware must import _only_ the cookie-names
module (which uses the `/cookies` subpaths). The classic trap: a
shared `lib/auth.ts` exporting both the engine and the names —
split them, as the example does.

## Session endpoint 401s with a live provider session

- **Unverified email.** Provider session exists, plugin linking
  refused. Verify the user (Better Auth: complete verification;
  Auth.js credentials: stamp `emailVerified`).
- **Missing origin (Auth.js / verifier).** Without `baseURL`
  (`AUTH_URL`) the internal session request falls back to the live
  `host`/`x-forwarded-host` headers. Proxies that strip host break
  it — and spoofed host headers would redirect the forwarded
  session cookie, so set the canonical origin in production
  instead of relying on the fallback.
- **Verifier returns `null` in development.** `createSessionVerifier`
  without `baseUrl` reads only the direct `Host` header (set
  `trustProxy: true` behind a local proxy) and only accepts
  `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]` (extend with
  `allowedDevelopmentHosts`). Rejections and timeouts are reported
  through `onError`. Outside `NODE_ENV=development` it throws at
  construction without `baseUrl`.
- **Clock skew.** Expiry checks run against the injected clock;
  wild skew reads as expired.

## Changes don't take effect locally

Stale `dist` — cross-package workspace imports resolve `dist`, not
`src` (same-package unit tests import `src` relatively and are
unaffected). `bun run build` after cross-package core changes. (The
`e2e` and `dev:example` scripts build first; ad-hoc `next dev` does
not.)

## Postgres parity run fails to boot

`bun run e2e:postgres` expects Postgres at `localhost:5433`
(`postgres` / `payload`): `docker run -d --name pal-pg -e
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=payload -p 5433:5432 postgres:16`. Override with
`PGHOST` / `PGPORT` / `PGUSER` / `PGPASSWORD` / `DATABASE_URL`.

## Mongo parity run throws lock/write conflicts

Single-node memory-server transients under concurrent transactions.
The example's mongo branch already disables transactions and uses
wiredTiger — if you re-enable transactions, expect `LockTimeout` /
`WriteConflict` flakes. Never "fix" these with product-code retries;
they are a test-environment artifact (real replica sets don't
behave this way).

## `attw` / `publint` failures on release

Run `bun run release:check`. `attw` must use `--profile esm-only`
(all packages are ESM-only by decision — legacy node10/CJS
resolution failures are the documented tradeoff). If `publint`
complains about missing files, check the package `files` list and
the `exports` map agree.

---

<!-- docs/upgrading.md -->

# Upgrading

Versioning rides [changesets](https://github.com/changesets/changesets):
every user-facing change ships a changeset, the release workflow
opens Version Packages PRs, and each package CHANGELOG records what
moved. This page covers the moves that need human attention —
especially database moves, where an unattended upgrade has historically
meant an unbootable app (see the per-adapter steps under each version
heading before you bump).

## Pre-1.0 policy

Minor versions may break: the wire contract (`SessionUser`, endpoint
paths, cookie semantics) is the stability anchor and changes only
with a migration note here; option shapes and internal ports may
evolve. Read the package CHANGELOGs on every bump.

The post-1.0 contract (what is public, semver per surface,
deprecation and security-fix policy) is in
[stability.md](stability.md); it takes effect at 1.0.

## Supported bands and the version assertion

The validated bands live in [compatibility.md](compatibility.md) and
equal the CI compat matrix ({floor, latest} per upstream). At wiring
time every package asserts the upstream versions it drives:

- the plugin checks `payload` (`supportedPayloadBand`),
- `provider-better-auth` checks `better-auth` (`supportedBetterAuthBand`),
- `provider-authjs` checks `@auth/core` (`supportedAuthJsBand`).

An out-of-band version throws `UnsupportedVersionError` (found vs
supported + a pointer here) **before any collection write** — an
unsupported upstream fails at startup with a typed, actionable error,
never as a raw SQL error or a missing-adapter `TypeError`
mid-request. When it fires: pin the upstream back inside the band
and wait for (or cut) a compat patch that widens the band after the
matrix proves the new version. Prerelease builds only ever match via
an explicit `exact` entry — canaries never float in through a range.

## plugin 0.14.0 / migrate 0.8.0 / provider-better-auth 0.11.0 / provider-authjs 0.7.0 (one minor across every package)

**Upgrade impact:** no database schema change; push and migrations have
nothing to do on SQLite, Postgres or MongoDB (the users collection gains
only an `afterRead` hook). The steps per package are below.

### provider-better-auth: two-factor step-up hardening (advisory GHSA-38wx-69j6-cgm7)

**Upgrade impact:** no schema change. The step-up counter reuses the
`failedVerificationCount` / `lockedUntil` columns Better Auth 1.7's
`twoFactor` model already has, so push and migrations have nothing to
do on SQLite, Postgres or MongoDB. Behaviour changes:

- **Step-ups share the sign-in lockout.** A `/two-factor/verify-*`
  on an existing session now spends the same per-user failure
  budget as the sign-in challenge (`twoFactor({ accountLockout })`,
  default 10 failures → locked 15 minutes). While locked, a step-up
  is refused with 429 `ACCOUNT_TEMPORARILY_LOCKED` before the code is
  checked, and failed step-ups can now lock the sign-in path too.
  Step-up UIs should handle the 429 like the sign-in screen does.
- **Enrolment no longer counts as MFA proof.** Confirming the FIRST
  factor (TOTP confirmation after `/two-factor/enable`, a backup code
  of an unconfirmed enrolment, the OTP that turns 2FA on) used to
  relabel the session `two-factor`. It now keeps its first-factor
  label, so a user who just enrolled still has MFA-gated roles
  withheld (`mfaRequired: true`) until they sign in again with 2FA or
  step up with the enrolled factor. If your enrolment screen sends
  users straight to an MFA-gated page, add that sign-in or step-up.
- **Emailed OTP after an inbox sign-in no longer proves MFA.** A
  `/two-factor/verify-otp` step-up relabels the session only after a
  `password` / `passkey` first factor. After a magic-link, email-OTP
  or OAuth sign-in (or an unrecorded method), it proves nothing; use
  TOTP or a backup code there. If your `otpOptions.sendOTP` delivers
  over an independent channel such as SMS, set
  `createBetterAuthEngine({ twoFactorOtpChannelIndependent: true })`.
- **Email-OTP sign-ins are recorded.** The provenance table now
  matches Better Auth 1.7's `/sign-in/email-otp` route, so these
  sessions report `methods: ['email-otp']` instead of `'unknown'`.
- Operator step: grant MFA-gated roles (`requireMfaForRoles`) only to
  users who have already enrolled 2FA. Enabling 2FA needs only the
  password, so a password-only attacker can still enrol their own
  authenticator on an account that never enrolled and then sign in
  with it.

### migrate: manifests bound to their database (advisory GHSA-crrr-3cg7-f6jw)

**Upgrade impact:** no collection schema change; push and migrations
have nothing to do on any adapter. The kit now writes two kinds of
records into Payload's key-value store (`payload-kv`; `payload_kv` on
SQL adapters) — this database's migration id and one record per run —
and REQUIRES that store for `--apply`, `adopt-prelink --apply`,
`rollback`, and `finalize` (it already required it for `finalize`).
If its table was never created, run your Payload migrations first.

**migrate**

- **Manifests are bound to their database and run (version 4).** The
  first `--apply` stores a random database id in `payload-kv`, and
  every run a random nonce; both are signed into the manifest. A
  manifest from another database (a rehearsal clone sharing
  `PAYLOAD_SECRET`), a run the database has no record of, or a copy of
  a manifest from before a rollback is refused before anything is
  written. Never roll back with a manifest from another environment or
  another run. A 0.7.x kit cannot read a version-4 manifest: do not
  downgrade the kit mid-migration.
- **Unsigned manifests are terminal.** A pre-0.6.0 (version 1/2) or
  0.6.0 manifest is never resumed by `--apply` / `adopt-prelink` and
  never re-signed: roll it back (`--allow-unsigned-manifest`) or
  finalize it, then start a new run with a new `--manifest`.
- **Plaintext prior values need their own flag.** A version-1
  manifest's plaintext values — including inside a manifest an older
  kit resumed and signed — are restored only with
  `--allow-plaintext-restore`, after you review them. A manifest
  holding any is never resumed.
- **0.7.0 manifests** (signed, no database binding) need
  `--allow-unbound-manifest` for `rollback` and for a resumed
  `--apply` / `adopt-prelink`; a resume binds them to the database it
  runs against.
  - Operator step, mid-migration on 0.7.0: run the 0.8.0 `rollback` or
    `--apply` against the SAME database the manifest was written
    against, with `--allow-unbound-manifest`. If you are not sure which
    database wrote it, do not pass the flag.
- **`rollback` refuses on ANY finalize marker** in the database (an
  import's or a pre-link's, whatever the manifest claims), and when the
  key-value store cannot be read (it used to log and trust the
  manifest's flag). An unsigned manifest may delete a `ba-users` row
  only when the host `users` document with that id exists.
- **The linking proof is opt-in.** `from-payload-auth --apply` and
  `adopt-prelink --apply` no longer grant `linkable` / `linkableEmail`
  from `emailVerified` by default — the flag can be stale for an
  address changed after it was verified, and the proof lets another
  provider's sign-in for the address link to the document
  (GHSA-v6mr). Every user still resolves through the pre-linked
  `better-auth` identity.
  - Operator step: to keep the old behaviour, review `emailVerified`
    first (no address changed since it was verified), then pass
    `--grant-linkable-from-verified`. Proofs granted by earlier runs
    are not revoked; re-check them as for `_verified` (plugin 0.13.0, below).
- **`verify` in adopt mode** now says it has nothing to compare and
  points to the checksum procedure ("Verifying an adopt cutover" in
  the migration guide), instead of failing on missing target
  collections or `baId`.
- **The doctor derives the source layout** from the loaded
  payload-auth config (custom slugs need no `--source-map` there) and
  prints it as a `--source-map` value for the other commands
  (`sourceMap` in `--json`).
- **Refused runs exit 1.** `from-payload-auth` and `adopt-prelink`
  print `<command> failed: …` and exit 1 when a manifest is refused.

### provider-better-auth: session tokens, logout cookie domain, adopt mode (issue #113)

**Upgrade impact:** no schema change. Push and migrations have nothing to
do on SQLite, Postgres or MongoDB. The operator steps are below.

- **Session tokens leave Better Auth's HTTP JSON.** `/get-session` no
  longer returns `session.token`, `/list-sessions` entries no longer
  carry `token`, and sign-in / sign-up (and other session-minting)
  bodies drop the new session's `token`. Server-side `auth.api.*`
  calls are unchanged. `/multi-session/*` and `/one-time-token/*` are
  untouched.
  - Operator step: client code that revokes one device with
    `authClient.revokeSession({ token: session.token })` should pass
    the listed id instead: `revokeSession({ token: session.id })`. The
    engine resolves the id server-side.
  - Operator step: a client that genuinely reads the raw token from a
    response body (a native app) sets the engine option
    `exposeSessionTokens: true`, ideally with
    `bearer({ requireSignature: true })`. Pass the engine a `logger` to
    see the new wiring warning when `bearer()` without
    `requireSignature` meets a token-exposing surface.
- **Adopt mode with Payload's local strategy on.** Better Auth sign-ups
  into an adopted users collection that keeps Payload's local strategy
  no longer fail with 422 "password" once other auth traffic has run
  first: every user create now carries the unusable injected password.
  No step needed.
- **Logout under `crossSubDomainCookies`.** The plugin's logout now
  clears every Better Auth cookie with the `Domain` Better Auth wrote
  it with (`crossSubDomainCookies.domain`, else the `baseURL`
  hostname); before, the browser kept the token and cookie-cache
  cookies until they expired. No step needed. With a dynamic `baseURL`,
  set `crossSubDomainCookies.domain` explicitly.

### plugin: account controls at authentication (advisory GHSA-mjvh-7vmj-pg2p)

**Upgrade impact:** no schema change. The users collection gains one
`afterRead` hook and no field, so push and migrations have nothing to
do on SQLite, Postgres or MongoDB. The behaviour changes and operator
checks are below.

**plugin**

- **A dead account's Payload credential no longer authenticates
  anything** (GHSA-mjvh-7vmj-pg2p). Suspension and the provider-owned
  local-credential default (GHSA-f4hj, GHSA-x45w) were enforced only
  at the users collection, the collection/global operation gates and
  the users permission map. A suspended user's Payload API key, an API
  key re-enabled by an operator on a provider-linked document, a
  pre-link local JWT on a host with `useSessions: false`, and a
  suspended user's local JWT still authenticated every surface that
  runs no collection operation: upload file routes
  (`/api/<upload>/file/<name>`), host custom endpoints (`req.user`),
  `payload.auth()`, `payload-preferences`, and `/access` grants on
  other collections. (The 0.13.0 note below said "`/access` grants it
  nothing"; that held for the users collection only.) Now such a
  credential resolves no user when Payload authenticates the request,
  so every surface sees an anonymous request. Provider sessions were
  never affected.
  - **Status codes change for these credentials.** The request is
    anonymous instead of refused: operations answer what an anonymous
    request gets from your access rules (usually 403 "You are not
    allowed to perform this action." where it used to be 401 "Account
    suspended", 401 "Local sessions are unavailable…", or 403 "API keys
    are unavailable…"), `GET /users/me` answers 200 with `user: null`,
    and `POST /users/refresh-token` answers 403. Local sign-in of a
    suspended or provider-linked account is still refused (401 / 403)
    as before. If a client keyed "sign in again" on that 401, also treat
    a 403 from a credential that used to work (or `me` → `user: null`)
    as signed out.
  - Host custom endpoints and `payload.auth()` callers now see
    `user: null` for these credentials. Nothing to change unless your
    code relied on seeing the suspended user.
  - Each refusal logs `local credential refused at authentication`
    (warn) with `userId`, `strategy` and `reason`.
  - Residual, documented in [security-model.md](security-model.md): a
    LIVE local credential holding a `requireMfaForRoles` role keeps the
    role on `req.user` inside a custom endpoint (operations and the
    users permission map withhold it). Check MFA with
    `sessionMfaSatisfied` / `denyWithoutMfa` in such endpoints.
- **A renamed `suspendedUntilField` is enforced for local
  credentials.** The local sign-in refusal, the reset refusal and the
  request-time gates read `suspendedUntil` literally, so with a renamed
  field a suspended user kept local sign-in, local JWTs and API keys
  (provider sessions were refused). They now read the configured
  field.
  - Operator step (renamed field only): review what suspended accounts
    did with local credentials while suspended.
- **The verified mirror follows the proof reset.** With
  `emailVerifiedField`, a self-service email change that resets the
  linking proof now also sets the mirror `false` (as `_verified` on
  verify hosts). It used to keep vouching for the new, unproven
  address.
- **Resolving an email-link collision is an operator decision.** The
  earlier guidance allowed granting `linkable` / `linkableEmail` after
  "a fresh verification of the current address". That proves who
  controls the address, not who built the document: on a squatted
  document the verification mail reaches the victim, and granting the
  proof on their click hands the victim's next sign-in the squatter's
  document. Grant the proof only for a document you confirmed is the
  address owner's own; otherwise rename or remove the document after
  checking who created it. The refusal log messages say so.
  - Operator step: if you granted the proof from verification clicks
    on documents that collided with a provider sign-in, check who
    created each of those documents.
- **Impersonation audit, two more records.** `onAudit` now receives
  `impersonated operation` with `operation: 'linkIdentity'` when
  verifying an impersonated session links or provisions the target's
  document, and with `operation: 'read'`,
  `endpoint: '/auth-link/organizations'` for the organization list
  read while impersonating (still allowed). Sinks that switch on
  `operation` should accept the new values.
- **`projectRolesAs: 'stored'` drops an unmappable role.** A role with
  no stored value is dropped (and logged) instead of reaching
  `req.user.roles` raw. Wiring through `authLink()` always maps every
  configured role, so this changes nothing for it.

### provider-authjs: builder `session` callbacks (issue #113)

Only apps that supply their own Auth.js `session` callback on the
database strategy are affected. The response is now scanned at every
depth: `sessionToken` keys and any string containing the live session
token are removed (array items that match are dropped), and the result
goes out in JSON form (`Date`s become ISO strings, as the client already
received them). A callback that returns a cyclic object fails with
`SESSION_SHAPE_INVALID`. Apps without a custom callback, and the JWT
strategy, are unaffected.

### Adopt mode: local strategy and MFA provenance (issue #113)

- provider-better-auth 0.11.0 injects an unknowable password into each
  create of an adopted users collection whose Payload local strategy is
  on, so sign-up and anonymous sign-in work. The doctor's
  `adopt-local-strategy-on` is now a warning. Turn the local strategy
  off unless break-glass operator accounts need it.
- Every adopted model is validated on the first adapter operation, so
  a missing or mis-mapped REQUIRED field now fails fast at boot.
  Previously it could go unnoticed until that model was used. A
  missing OPTIONAL Better Auth field (for example 1.7's
  `jwks.expiresAt` on a payload-auth layout) is tolerated: writes to it
  are dropped.
- An adopted session collection without an `authenticationMethod`
  field records no MFA provenance, so `requireMfaForRoles` stays
  withheld (fail closed). Add a text field named `authenticationMethod` to it if you use
  MFA-gated roles.

## plugin 0.13.0 / migrate 0.7.0 / provider-better-auth 0.10.0 / provider-authjs 0.6.0 (one minor across every package)

**Upgrade impact:** no schema change. Push and migrations have nothing to
do on SQLite, Postgres or MongoDB. The operator steps are below.

**plugin**

- **Payload API keys on provider-linked documents.** With
  `auth.useAPIKey`, linking a provider identity now clears the
  document's API key. A key on a linked document, including one
  enabled after the link, is refused (403) on every collection and
  global, and the users collection's `/access` entry grants it nothing
  (other surfaces: see the GHSA-mjvh section above). Documents without linked
  identities are unaffected. To keep keys working during a migration,
  set `allowLocalCredentialsForLinkedDocs: true` and remove it once the
  migration is done.
  - Operator step: move service integrations that use a linked user's
    API key to an unlinked service account.
- **Granting the linking proof.** Do not grant `linkable` /
  `linkableEmail` based on `_verified`. Grant it only from an
  operator-reviewed list that confirms the DOCUMENT belongs to the
  owner of its current address, checked against the current email.
  (This note used to also allow "a fresh verification of the current
  address" — withdrawn, see the GHSA-mjvh section above: a
  verification proves the address, not the document.) The earlier
  snippet that granted it from `_verified` is withdrawn.
  - If you ran that snippet, re-check the documents it touched.
  - Refusal logs now say to resolve an email collision (confirm the
    owner, then rename or remove the conflicting document).
- **Organization endpoints under impersonation.** `POST
/auth-link/organizations`, `/invite` and `/accept` now answer every
  impersonated call with the audited 403. That includes calls where the
  impersonated user's session does not verify, which used to answer
  401 without an audit record.
- **`authLinkServer(payload)` across module copies.** The server
  registry is now shared by every loaded copy of the plugin. Under
  TanStack Start, an API route no longer throws
  `AuthLinkServerMissingError` when `/admin` booted Payload first.

**provider-authjs**

- **Session JSON shape.** The Auth.js session endpoint (`GET
{basePath}/session`) now returns an allowlisted shape on both session
  strategies: `{ user: { name, email, image, id, emailVerified },
expires }`.
  - A custom `session` callback keeps every field it returns except
    `sessionToken`, `userId` and `id`, which are always removed.
  - Client code that read those fields from the session JSON must get
    what it needs from your own `session` callback.

**provider-better-auth**

- **Logout cookies.** Logout now also expires the cookie-cache and
  `account_data` chunk cookies (`<name>.0` … `<name>.N`).
- **In-session MFA step-up.** A correct second factor on an existing
  session now always marks that session MFA-proven. Apps using
  `requireMfaForRoles` get the roles back after an in-session TOTP
  step-up.
- **`not_in` and NULL.** `not_in` on nullable fields now keeps NULL
  rows, matching Better Auth's memory adapter. Bulk updates and deletes
  that use `not_in` may now affect more rows.
- **Non-ASCII email matching.** Case-insensitive `eq` now matches
  non-ASCII text on SQLite.
- **`verifyApiKey` owners.** It refuses organization-owned keys and keys
  of deleted users with `UnsupportedApiKeyOwnerError`.

**migrate**

- **`finalize`.** It now needs `--config`. It records the finalize in
  the app's database (Payload's `payload-kv`) and re-signs the
  manifest. Rollback is refused afterwards, whatever the file says.
  The manifest signature now covers `finalized`.
- **`rollback`.**
  - It only deletes rows in the import's own target collections. Pass
    the same `--slugs` the import used.
  - A delete that fails exits non-zero, names the rows and keeps the
    manifest.
  - `--allow-unsigned-manifest` no longer deletes rows. Add
    `--allow-unsigned-deletes` after reviewing a pre-0.6.0 manifest's
    created rows.
  - To roll back with a 0.6.0 manifest, pass `--allow-unsigned-manifest`.
- **`export`.** It takes `--source-map`. It exits 1 when a mapped table
  is missing (map a model to `null` if it isn't installed), and now
  includes child, plugin, `ba_*` and `oauth_*` tables. Progress goes to
  stderr.
- **Other fixes.**
  - `verify` checks the configured roles field.
  - A second `--apply` is a true no-op.
  - The doctor finds `genericOAuth` under nested import paths.
  - A new doctor blocker flags adopt mode with Payload's local strategy
    on. In adopt mode, set `auth: { disableLocalStrategy: true }` on the
    users collection.

## plugin 0.12.0 / migrate 0.6.0 (one minor across every package)

**Upgrade impact:** no schema change; nothing to run on any adapter.
No option was added or removed.

- **migrate: signed manifests.** `--apply` and `adopt-prelink` now
  write a version-3 manifest carrying an HMAC keyed from the app's
  `PAYLOAD_SECRET`. `rollback`, and a resumed `--apply` /
  `adopt-prelink`, refuse a manifest that fails the check (an edited
  file could otherwise delete arbitrary rows or set allowlisted fields
  such as `roles`). **If you are mid-migration** with a manifest
  written by migrate ≤ 0.5.x, the first `rollback` or resumed run needs
  `--allow-unsigned-manifest`; the next write signs it. A version-2
  manifest holding a plaintext value is refused even then.
- **plugin: `readVersions` default on the users collection.** When the
  host leaves it unset, user versions are readable by role managers
  only (Payload's default let any signed-in user list every user's
  versions, emails included, on a users collection with `versions`).
  Declare `access.readVersions` to keep a different policy.
- **plugin: `roleValues` on local sessions.** The role-manager check
  and the `requireMfaForRoles` strip now compare canonical roles for
  every session. A local session holding a mapped policy role (say
  stored `AUDITOR` for `auditor`) now loses it without MFA, as an
  unmapped one always did. A local admin whose manager role is stored
  under another value is now a role manager.
- Payload 3.91.0 is the tested `latest` on v3 (the peer range is
  unchanged).

## plugin 0.11.x patches (after the hardening release)

**Upgrade impact:** no schema change; nothing to run on any adapter.

- `req.user.id` for provider sessions now has the database's own id type
  (a number on SQLite/Postgres). Code comparing it with `===` against a
  string id should compare `String(id)`; Payload's own relationship
  writes (v4's `createdBy`/`updatedBy`) now accept it.
- The users collection gains a `me` hook: for auth-link sessions
  presented as `Authorization: Bearer` (`admitChannels` with
  `'bearer'`), `GET /api/users/me` answers with the verified session's
  `exp` and never returns the provider token as `token` (it used to
  500). Cookie sessions and other strategies are unchanged.
- `authLinkServer(payload).revokeSession` with an Auth.js database
  session engine now throws for a handle that matches no session.

## plugin 0.11.0 / provider-better-auth 0.8.0 / web 0.3.0 / migrate 0.5.0 (hardening release)

One minor release across every package (core 0.7.0, next 0.4.0,
react 0.3.0, tanstack-start 0.3.0, provider-authjs 0.4.0 too). No
schema change. Read each section before you bump.

### Users-collection write defaults

**Upgrade impact:** no schema change; access defaults only.

1. **Users `update` and `delete` are no longer open to every signed-in
   user.** When your users collection declares no `access.update`, the
   plugin now allows a user to update only their own document (role
   managers: every document); with no `access.delete`, only role
   managers delete users. Neither is allowed while impersonating.
   Payload's own default (`Boolean(req.user)`) let any signed-in user
   (with JIT sign-up, anyone) rewrite or delete any user, including
   re-pointing a local admin's email and resetting its password. If
   you relied on the open default, declare the access you want
   explicitly.
2. **A non-manager only ever changes their own email**, even when your
   collection-level `update` is broader.
3. **`unlock` is role managers only** by default (it was any signed-in
   user).
4. **`migrate export --out` and the import manifest are written
   owner-only (0600)**, tightened before content lands. Manifest
   values are bound to their entry, and rollback restores only the
   fields the kit writes (`identities`, `roles`, `linkable`,
   `linkableEmail`, `updatedAt`).
5. **`sessionEndpoint` values with whitespace or control characters
   throw** `InvalidConfigError` (URL parsing would strip them and could
   resolve the path protocol-relative).

### Organization governance; `_verified` is not linking proof

**Upgrade impact:** no schema change. No column is added, removed,
or retyped (the users snapshot is unchanged; the memberships
collection only gains field access and hooks), so push and
migrations both have nothing to do on SQLite, Postgres, and MongoDB.
The changes are behavioural; read each before you bump.

1. **Payload's `_verified` no longer admits a document to JIT email
   linking on its own.** Only the plugin's `linkable` proof bound to
   the current address (`linkableEmail`) does — what
   [security-model.md](security-model.md) row 8 always documented.
   Payload keeps `_verified` across email changes (and its default
   field access lets any signed-in user write it), so a verified
   document re-pointed at someone else's address used to inherit
   their provider identity. **Operator step:** if you relied on
   `_verified` alone for pre-existing host accounts, do NOT backfill
   the proof from `_verified`. Before this release a self-service
   email change kept `_verified`, and the proof reset only applies to
   email changes made after the upgrade, so a document verified
   before the upgrade may carry `_verified: true` for an address it
   never proved — granting it the proof would link that address's
   owner's next sign-in to a document they may not own. Grant `linkable` +
   `linkableEmail` only from **an operator-reviewed, explicit list**
   of documents, each confirmed to BELONG to the owner of its current
   address (who created it, what it holds), re-checked at write time.
   A fresh verification of the current email is NOT enough (an
   earlier version of this note allowed it): it proves who controls
   the ADDRESS, not who built the DOCUMENT. On a squatted document —
   one someone else created with, or re-pointed at, the victim's
   address — the verification mail reaches the victim, and one click
   would hand the victim's next sign-in that document (its local
   password, API key, data, and anything else planted on it). The
   reviewed list, applied:

   ```ts
   // Each entry was reviewed by an operator: the document AND the
   // address confirmed to belong to its owner today. Never build this
   // list from `_verified`.
   const reviewed: { id: string | number; email: string }[] = [/* … */]
   for (const entry of reviewed) {
     const doc = await payload.findByID({ collection: 'users', id: entry.id, overrideAccess: true })
     if (doc.email.toLowerCase() !== entry.email.toLowerCase()) {
       continue // the email changed since the review: re-review it
     }
     await payload.update({
       collection: 'users',
       id: entry.id,
       data: { linkable: true, linkableEmail: doc.email },
       overrideAccess: true,
     })
   }
   ```

   Anything else stays unproven: its address owner's sign-in is
   refused (logged) until the collision is resolved.

   The migration importer (`@payload-auth-link/migrate`) already
   grants `linkable` + `linkableEmail` from verified emails and is
   unaffected. A refused link whose provisioning then collides with
   the existing document now logs
   `provisioning refused: the email is held by an existing document
that is not proven to own it` and answers a typed 401 (it used to
   surface as a storage error). Resolve such a collision as an operator:
   confirm who created and owns the existing document, and rename or
   remove it when it is not the address owner's. Never resolve it by
   sending a verification mail, and grant the proof only for a
   document you confirmed is the address owner's own.

2. **A self-service email change resets the proof.** Changing a
   document's email in any write that is neither the plugin's
   provider-email resync nor a role manager's clears `linkable` and
   `linkableEmail`, and — on `auth.verify` hosts — `_verified`. Users
   who change their own email on a verify host must re-verify before
   local sign-in works again (Payload does not resend the
   verification mail by itself; trigger it from your app).

3. **Linking revokes earlier local sessions.** When a provider
   identity links to a document, Payload's `sessions` array for it is
   cleared (`auth.useSessions`, Payload's default), so a local JWT
   issued before the link is refused on its next request. Hosts with
   `useSessions: false` get the same outcome from the account-control
   gate, which now refuses `local-jwt` requests on provider-linked
   documents (401) unless `allowLocalCredentialsForLinkedDocs` is set.

4. **Organization governance.** With `organizations.enabled`:
   memberships can no longer change `organization` or `user` after
   create (REST writes to them are dropped; Local-API writes throw);
   role writes never exceed the caller's own org role (an `admin`
   cannot create, promote to, or edit an owner); the last active
   owner of an organization cannot be demoted or removed (`409`);
   `DELETE /api/organizations/:id` cascades the organization's
   memberships and invitations instead of failing; and every
   organization write, membership write, invite, and acceptance is
   refused (`403`) and audited while impersonating. Seed scripts that
   re-pointed memberships through the Local API must delete and
   re-create the row instead.

5. **Organization write scoping.** Also with `organizations.enabled`:
   - Bulk `PATCH`/`DELETE /api/organizations?where=…` only reaches
     organizations the caller manages (owns, for delete). A request
     body field no longer decides which organization authorizes the
     write.
   - Deleting an organization is owner-only. An org `admin` now gets
     `403`.
   - `verifiedDomains` can be written only by Payload role managers
     (`roleManagerRoles`), and not while impersonating. Org owners and
     admins who set domains through REST or the admin panel will see
     the field ignored. Review existing `verifiedDomains` entries once
     after upgrading, because before this release any organization
     creator could list any domain.
   - Removing or demoting an owner now writes the organization row
     first (it bumps `updatedAt`). This serializes concurrent owner
     removals.
   - Accepting an invitation after already joining the organization
     answers `409` instead of a storage validation error.

### Session verifier, logout, and redirect hardening

No schema change. Behavior changes that may need attention:

1. **`createSessionVerifier` requires `baseUrl` unless
   `NODE_ENV === 'development'`.** It used to fall back to the
   request's host headers on every runtime that was not `production`
   (test, staging, preview, unset). Those now throw
   `InvalidConfigError` at construction — pass `baseUrl` (or an
   absolute `sessionEndpoint`). In development the fallback ignores
   `X-Forwarded-Host`/`-Proto` unless you set `trustProxy: true`,
   only accepts `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, and `[::1]` (extend with
   `allowedDevelopmentHosts`), and protocol-relative `sessionEndpoint`
   values throw. The verifier's fetch now times out after
   `timeoutMs` (default 5000) and no longer follows redirects; both
   fail closed. `resolveSessionUrl`'s host fallback now defaults to
   off, and `resolveOrigin` (core) honors forwarded headers only with
   `trustProxy`.
2. **`safeRedirectPath` returns the normalised path.** Dot segments
   resolve before the API-prefix and sign-in checks, so
   `/x/../api/...` and `/./sign-in` fall back, and a benign
   `/x/../account` comes back as `/account`.
3. **Logout expires more cookies.** `DELETE /api/auth-link/session`
   also expires Better Auth's `dont_remember` and cookie-cache
   `session_data` cookies, the `__Secure-`/plain counterpart of every
   name, and the configured `legacySessions` names. A logout that
   presents no session cookie (and no `Authorization`/`x-api-key`
   header) answers without querying any provider — still the
   idempotent `401` with the clearing cookies.
4. **Provider login view paths follow your config.** The break-glass
   form posts to `${routes.api}/${usersCollection}/login` and lands on
   `routes.admin`; set `admin.signInPath`/`admin.authBase` when your
   sign-in page or Better Auth mount differs from `/sign-in` and
   `/api/auth`. The import map needs no regeneration (same
   component, new props).
5. **React provider sequencing.** Only the newest session read writes
   state; `signOut` aborts in-flight reads. `fetchSession` accepts an
   optional `AbortSignal`.

## 0.10.x → 0.11.0 (recorded sign-in methods; opaque session handles)

Two changes to the server-session surface, both driven by the
post-release review (issues #79 and #80).

1. **Better Auth's own sign-in flows record their authentication
   method.** 0.10.1's assurance read the per-session
   `authenticationMethod` column, but only server-side mints wrote it —
   a user completing Better Auth's NATIVE two-factor sign-in got
   `mfa: 'unknown'` and `requireMfaForRoles` withheld their role. The
   provenance plugin now stamps the method on every sign-in flow it
   recognizes (`password`, `two-factor` on the verification endpoints,
   `oauth` callbacks, `magic-link`, `email-otp`, `passkey`); unknown
   paths still record nothing (fail closed). Apps on 0.10.1/0.7.1
   needing MFA roles through a custom step-up route can drop it after
   upgrading — the native flow now works. BA's 2FA-pending sign-in
   expires the session cookie, so a single-factor session is never
   relabelled: the second factor issues a FRESH session, recorded as
   `two-factor`.

2. **Session ids are opaque handles, never bearer tokens.**
   `listSessions` and `createSessionFor().sessionId` used to return
   the raw session token — a "sign out other sessions" page would have
   put a live credential for every session into page data. They now
   return the session ROW id; `revokeSession` resolves the id to the
   token server-side (BA's own logout internals, which revoke by
   token, are unaffected). `createSessionFor().token` is unchanged —
   the token still rides exactly where setting the cookie needs it.
   **`sessionCookie(token)` still takes the TOKEN** (the mint
   response's `token` field), not the id.

## 0.10.x → 0.10.1 (server-session API hardening; advisory GHSA-hxgq-9pww-59j4)

Four fixes to the server session API, all fail-closed.

1. **Minted sessions no longer claim MFA.** Session assurance now
   reads a per-session record of HOW the session came into being —
   the engine appends an internal plugin that adds one nullable
   `authenticationMethod` column to the session table (additive; rows
   that predate it read as "no recorded method"). A server-side mint
   records `server-mint` and reports `mfa: false` — it ran no 2FA
   challenge. The old read leaned on `user.twoFactorEnabled`
   (ENROLLMENT), so every mint for an enrolled user claimed a second
   factor that never ran. **`requireMfaForRoles` sites**: sign-in
   sessions now report `mfa: 'unknown'` until a flow records a
   method — the gate treats `'unknown'` as absent (fail-closed), so
   gated roles stay withheld for plain cookie sign-ins. To restore
   them, mint with the new `createSessionFor(userId, { mfaProof:
true })` — set it ONLY when the server has itself verified a
   second factor; the session then records `server-step-up` and
   reports `mfa: true`. **Schema note:** the engine adds the session
   column through Better Auth's own schema machinery; run your usual
   Payload push/migrations on upgrade (additive column, no data
   changes).
2. **One id type across mint/list/revoke — the session token.**
   `listSessions` and `createSessionFor` used to hand out session ROW
   ids while revocation deleted by TOKEN, so revoking a listed id
   deleted nothing and reported success. Both now return tokens (the
   id `createSessionFor` returns revokes directly), and revocation is
   verified in both directions: revoking an id with no session behind
   it is an ERROR (nothing was deleted), and a delete that leaves the
   row in place is an error too.
3. **The requested TTL is honored and the STORED expiry is audited.**
   The mint passed its expiry into Better Auth's `dontRememberMe`
   parameter slot (a truthy Date), so every minted session got the
   engine's default expiry (~24h) no matter what was requested — and
   the audit event recorded the requested value as if stored. The mint
   now passes the expiry through Better Auth's `override` (applied
   with `overrideAll`), and the audit event and returned `expiresAt`
   carry the expiry the provider actually stored.
4. **`'dev-only'` means development.** The `allowServerSessions`
   default enabled minting on every runtime that merely wasn't
   `production` — CI, test, staging, unset. It now enables minting
   ONLY when `NODE_ENV === 'development'`; every other runtime
   refuses with `ServerSessionsDisabledError`. Set `allowServerSessions:
true` explicitly where minting is intended outside development.

## 0.9.x → 0.10.0 (the server-session kit's correctness pass)

Fixes from the first production rehearsal (issues #68–#72). Three of
them change behaviour that previously "worked" by silently doing
nothing.

1. **`sessionCookie` is signed — and async.** Better Auth reads the
   session token cookie with `getSignedCookie` ONLY, so the
   server-session API's cookie must be `token.<HMAC signature>`.
   0.9.0 minted the raw token, which Better Auth refused (every
   bridge built on `createSessionFor().setCookie` or
   `authLinkServer.sessionCookie()` logged nobody in). The cookie is
   now built from the engine's own resolved context (secret, name,
   `Secure`/`SameSite`/`Path`/`Max-Age` attributes). **Type change:**
   `sessionCookie(token)` returns `Promise<string>` on
   `authLinkServer` and on the provider port — `await` it. A
   real-engine round trip (mint → setCookie → `getSession` resolves
   the user) pins the behaviour.

2. **`legacySessions` on the plugin now enforces agreement.** The
   plugin option never enabled anything — the provider ENGINE's
   `legacySessions` input is what honors legacy cookies. Wiring now
   throws `InvalidConfigError` when the plugin option is set but no
   engine declares a window, when the two disagree on `until` or
   `cookieNames`, or when a legacy cookie name collides with a
   current session cookie name. Engine-only configuration stays
   legal. If you set only the plugin option believing it bounded the
   window, move the window to `createBetterAuthEngine({
legacySessions })` (and keep the plugin option identical, if you
   want the assertion).

3. **`revokeAllForUser` revokes on every linked provider.** It used
   to walk only the first capable identity; a user linked to two
   providers kept the second provider's sessions. It now attempts
   every linked provider and throws if any fails.

4. **The provider login view actually renders.** The `loginView:
'provider'` registration was missing its `exportName`, so
   Payload's import map never resolved it (empty login page), and its
   provider link pointed at `/api/auth/sign-in`, which is not a
   Better Auth route. The view now registers as
   `@payload-auth-link/plugin/admin#ProviderLoginView` and signs in
   through Better Auth's own `POST /sign-in/email`; the break-glass
   local form is unchanged. **Apps enabling `admin: { loginView:
'provider' }` must regenerate the import map** (`payload
generate:importmap`) after upgrading — a stale map still renders
   an empty page.

5. **Stray debug output removed.** The server session API printed
   `DBG …` lines to stdout on every identity resolution; gone.

## 0.6.x → 0.7.0 (account controls on every strategy; provider-owned documents)

Three default-behaviour changes, all fail-closed. The full
credential-path matrix now lives in
[security-model.md](security-model.md).

1. **Suspension is enforced on every strategy, at request time.**
   Previously only the `auth-link` strategy checked `suspendedUntil`;
   a user with a local password (Payload's own `login` / local JWT /
   API key) kept working after being suspended. Now `beforeLogin`
   refuses the local sign-in (401), and a request-time gate on every
   collection and global refuses any request carrying a suspended
   account's local JWT or API key (401) — including `refresh-token`,
   and including GraphQL. Nothing to migrate; sites that suspended
   users get the behaviour the field always promised.

2. **`policies.requireMfaForRoles` now applies to local credentials.**
   Local sessions have no MFA proof, so a role listed in the policy is
   withheld from local-strategy sessions (JWT, API key) at request
   time — before access checks read the roles. Local login itself is
   NOT blocked; the session simply loses the gated role. The
   `/access` permission map is truthful for the users collection;
   host collections' maps can still overstate (their access functions
   are the host's) but no operation honors it.

3. **Provider-linked documents are provider-owned** (new default, new
   option `allowLocalCredentialsForLinkedDocs`, default `false`):
   once a document holds linked provider identities, local sign-in is
   refused (403) and the forgot/reset-password flow is refused (403,
   no token is issued) for it. A local password on such a document
   would bypass the provider's MFA, bans, rate limits, and
   revocation. Documents WITHOUT linked identities — operator
   accounts, imports not yet linked — keep local credentials and the
   recovery flow exactly as before. This affects the
   payload-auth migration runbook: an imported user's password works
   until their provider identity links; after that the provider owns
   the credential. Sites needing both credentials alive during a
   migration window set `allowLocalCredentialsForLinkedDocs: true`
   and remove it when the migration completes.

No schema changes; no backfill. The credential-path matrix test
(`integration-credential-paths.test.ts`) pins all three.

## 0.1.1 → 0.2.0

What changed in the database (and nothing else did — provider
collection shapes otherwise moved zero columns):

- **`users`** gains three optional governance fields: `phone`
  (text), `suspendedUntil` (date), `suspendReason` (text). All
  nullable and additive — safe on every adapter, every mode.
- **`aj-verification-tokens`** (Auth.js provider): `token` loses its
  standalone unique index; a new nullable unique `key` column
  identifies a token by its `(identifier, token-hash)` pair. This is
  the composite-key fix: the same OTP hash may now exist for two
  different identifiers. The `key` column is **nullable** — pre-fix
  releases shipped it `required`, which is what made upgraded
  databases unbootable (see below); 0.2.1+ accepts `NULL` keys and
  backfills lazily on write.
- **`ba-*` collections** (Better Auth provider): no shape change.

Verification tokens are **not** invalidated: existing rows keep
working (the adapter reads by `(identifier, token)` and tolerates
`NULL` keys). No data loss on any adapter.

**SQLite, dev-push (Payload `push: true`):** just boot the new
version. Adding a nullable column alters the table in place — no
data-loss prompt, no table rebuild. (0.2.0 exactly shipped `key` as
required; booting it hangs on drizzle's data-loss prompt and can
recreate the token table empty. Upgrade straight to 0.2.1+.)

**Postgres, dev-push:** same — the column adds in place and the
unique index swaps `token` → `key`. (0.2.0 exactly hung on the same
prompt; Postgres converged if you accepted, but the token table
emptied.)

**Production (migrations mode):** generate the migration yourself
(`payload.migrate:create`) and check it adds `key` as a **nullable**
column and drops the `token` unique index — `ADD COLUMN key TEXT`
without `NOT NULL`. On a non-empty table, a NOT NULL variant fails
outright (`column "key" contains null values`); a nullable one is a
no-loss step. See the [migrations recipe](#running-production-on-migrations-not-push).

**MongoDB:** schema drift cannot crash Mongo, but index lifecycle is
the trap: Payload's adapter never drops indexes, so the **stale
`token` unique index survives the upgrade** (silently keeping the
pre-0.2.0 "one row per token hash" constraint), and the added `key`
unique index builds in the background over rows without the field.
Fix with the idempotent reconciliation helper:

```ts
import { reconcileAuthJsMongoIndexes } from '@payload-auth-link/provider-authjs'

const report = await reconcileAuthJsMongoIndexes(payload)
// { status: 'reconciled', droppedStaleTokenIndex, backfilledKeys, keyIndex }
```

It backfills `key` (`JSON.stringify([identifier, tokenHash])`),
drops the stale `token` unique index, and reports (rather than
throws) when the `key` index build is still in flight. Run it once
per deployment after upgrading (idempotent; safe to re-run).
Already upgraded without it? The composite-key behavior silently
does not hold on your deployment until you run the reconciliation.

## 0.4.0 → 0.5.0 users, continued in 0.5.x → 0.6.0 (proof bound to the email)

Follow-up to the JIT-linking proof above: the `linkable` marker is now
bound to the email it was granted for (new `linkableEmail` field). The
proof holds only while the document email equals `linkableEmail`:

- Self-service email changes over REST on documents with linked
  identities are role-manager-only (stripped for non-managers), and
  self-service local passwords on plugin-managed documents are
  stripped — one document can no longer hold two independently owned
  credentials, and a local credential can no longer bypass Better
  Auth's MFA/bans/verification.
- The plugin's provider-email resync keeps the proof in step
  (repository `setEmail` moves both the email and the proof, with
  `overrideAccess`).
- Linking to a document that also holds a local password now warns
  (the hidden-field lookup that previously never fired is fixed).

**Backfill for existing `linkable: true` documents** (created by
