- `@scope/plugin` — Payload server: plugin fn, collections/globals
  extension, AuthStrategy, endpoints, hooks, access, `admin/`.
  Depends on core + payload.
- `@scope/react` — provider-agnostic UI (sign-in buttons, user menu,
  admin helpers). No Next, no Payload imports.
- `@scope/next` — Next.js adapter: route handlers, middleware/proxy,
  cookie/session helpers. Depends on core + react.
- `@scope/provider-<id>` — one package per identity provider.
  Initial build: `better-auth` first, `authjs` after its spike (both shipped, Phase 4).
  `workos` and `clerk` deferred post-v1 (SaaS-backed, not locally
  validatable); the registry reserves their ids.
- `examples/basic` — reference integration and e2e target (SQLite,
  self-seeding, like onpage's `:3100` example).

### v1 ports

- `UserRepository` — users via Payload Local API (never raw DB).
- `SessionPort` — verify/create/revoke sessions; strategies delegate here.
- `IdentityProviderPort` — per-IdP authorize/callback/webhook/profile
  normalize; instances registered in an adapter registry keyed by id.
- `CookiePort` — read/write/clear; implemented by the framework adapter.
- `TransactionPort`, `LoggerPort`, `TracerPort` — storage transactions,
  structured logs, spans. `ClockPort` + `IdPort` for determinism.

### Dependency rules (lint-enforced via `no-restricted-imports`)

- core imports no framework. react imports no Next/Payload.
  plugin imports no React outside `admin/`.
- Sources import siblings with `.ts`/`.tsx` extensions.
- Cross-package imports use workspace package names, never deep paths
  outside declared subpath exports.

## 2. Payload contract

- Plugin shape: `definePlugin<TOptions>({ slug, order, plugin })`;
  `(options) => (incomingConfig) => Config`. Copy config, spread-append
  collections/globals, merge hook objects (never overwrite), chain
  `onInit`, return config. Lower `order` first; cross-plugin via `plugins` map.
- Auth strategy: `{ name, authenticate({ headers, payload, req, ... }) }`
  returning `{ user: { ...doc, collection } } | null`. Read-only session
  checks use refresh-disabled reads (no login loops).
- `auth.strategies[]` plus explicit cookies/token/api-key options.
- Custom `endpoints[]` are unauthenticated by default: check `req.user`,
  method lowercase, `handler(req: PayloadRequest) => Response`.
  Every state-changing endpoint gets a CSRF guard + access check —
  authorization goes through one `access.ts` using Payload's access ops.
- Preserve existing hooks when extending (append, don't replace);
  inject admin/meta fields as a group. Root/collection/global/field
  hooks are awaited in series; `afterError` may transform.
- Admin UI is React Server Components by default; `'use client'` only
  where needed, registered as `{ path#Export, clientProps/serverProps }`.
- Migrations are host-owned (`up`/`down`, `migrate:create/status/down`).
  The plugin ships no migration mechanism.

## 3. Coupling guardrails (the payload-auth anti-patterns, banned)

- No double-pass init: resolve schemas once, before hooks/endpoints/
  `useAsTitle` attach — never build-collections → sync → rebuild.
- No monkey-patch contract: no `Object.defineProperty(payload, …)`,
  no string flags on `config.custom`, no per-invocation client
  re-entry from strategies/hooks/endpoints. Typed injected client
  from the composition root instead.
- No framework leak: no `next/headers` (or any framework import)
  inside Payload hooks or core. Cookie/transport work lives in the
  framework adapter (`toNextJsHandler`, `nextCookies()`).
- No stringly schema map: typed slug/field maps with explicit errors.
  No silent fallbacks, no "warns but uses wrong slug", no runtime
  patching of provider internals.
- No hand-rolled sessions: no admin-session hacks, manual `Set-Cookie`
  concat, or fabricated endpoint contexts. Sessions go through
  `SessionPort` + `CookiePort`.

## 4. Type safety

- `strict` plus `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`,
  `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, `verbatimModuleSyntax`, `noUnused*`.
  Guard indexes; never assert (`!`). Options filled from other
  optionals are typed `?: T | undefined`.
- Zero-`any` boundary: no `: any`, no `as` casts at module edges,
  no whole-instance erasure (`as unknown as …`). Sanitize by deep-copy,
  never shallow-spread-then-deep-write the caller's options.
- Generics survive: provider/plugin options preserve their type
  parameters end to end (no hardcoded generated-types artifact that
  silently drops endpoints when plugins change).
- One canonical `Role` type with a smart constructor at the boundary.
  No `array | string | comma-string` branching at every call site;
  normalize once, use everywhere.
- Make the compiler check it: discriminated unions + `assertNever`,
  branded keys for document refs, readiness guards before reading
  loaded state, typed message catalogs for UI strings.

## 5. Errors and validation

- Expected failures return `neverthrow` `Result<T, E>` /
  `ResultAsync` (`ok`/`err`, `fromThrowable`, `combine`,
  `fromPromise`/`fromSafePromise`). Throw only for the truly unexpected.
- Domain errors vs application errors stay distinct
  (`InvalidEmailError` vs `UserExistsError`); the web adapter maps
  them to status codes. Never swallow (`null`/`[]`/`0` on failure),
  never drop nulls, never leave endpoints unauthenticated by accident.
- Validate at every untyped boundary with Zod
  (`safeParse`/`safeParseAsync`, `z.infer`, `.strict()`).
  Zod over TypeBox: distinct `z.input`/`z.output` and superior error
  reporting matter more here than schema-reuse speed, and validation
  sits off the session hot path.
- Startup validation fails fast: baseURL/secret present, default role
  inside roles, adapter-boundary schemas valid.

## 6. Observability

- Domain depends on `LoggerPort` + `TracerPort` only. Adapters use
  pino (child loggers per module, `serializers.err`, never untrusted
  keys) and OpenTelemetry spans, injected — never imported.
- No `console.*` anywhere. Forward into Payload's pino instance and
  the provider logger where supported.
- No hardcoded query depth: depth is configurable per call site.
- Transactions go through `TransactionPort` — no no-op stubs.

## 7. Testing constitution (e2e is mandatory)

- Unit tests live next to code in `src/__tests__/`.
- Integration tests run real Payload on in-memory SQLite through
  `handleEndpoints` (onpage precedent), or the Local API over a
  memory DB with fixtures (`config`, `resetBetweenTests`).
- Behavior change → test. Security change → an integration test
  that fails without the fix.
- Playwright e2e runs against `examples/basic` with a fresh DB:
  sign-in, OAuth callback, webhook user-sync, logout, session
  revoke from the admin, role-gated access. Chromium, retries on CI,
  traces retained on failure, axe for admin UI regressions.
- DB strategy: SQLite in-memory for local/unit, `mongodb-memory-server`
  replica set for integration default, containerized Postgres for
  parity in CI.
- `bun run check` gates everything: format, lint, typecheck,
  coverage thresholds, build, size budgets. No merge on red.

## 8. Repo conventions

- Bun monorepo: `packages/*` + `examples/*` workspaces, `tsc -b` build,
  `publint` + `are-the-types-wrong` on publishable packages.
- Prettier: single quotes, no semicolons, width 100.
  typescript-eslint type-checked, react-hooks, jsx-a11y.
- Changesets required for user-facing changes; provenance-enabled
  publishes; `SECURITY.md` for private reports.
- Public API → TSDoc plus `docs/` guides. Docs follow the onpage
  system as they grow: tour, getting-started, concepts, guides,
  compatibility, troubleshooting, upgrading — plus `llms.txt` and
  `AGENTS.md` for agent consumers.
- Never commit secrets, never log credentials, never ship a release
  with debug output (release hygiene is a checklist item, not a hope).

## 9. Security invariants

- Never link a provider identity to an existing user, or reuse an
  existing email for a provider login, unless the provider verified the
  email (`emailVerified`). Unverified profiles must not take over
  existing accounts; creation of a standalone user is the provider's
  verification lifecycle to complete.
- State-changing endpoints require CSRF proof: matching `Origin` or a
  custom header a cross-site page cannot set. Redirect targets are
  validated same-origin against `baseUrl` — never an open redirect.

---

<!-- docs/PLAN.md -->

## Goal

Replace `payload-auth/payload-auth` with a greenfield Payload CMS v3
plugin: hexagonal ports/adapters, strict typesafe, enterprise grade,
where Better Auth (first) and Auth.js/NextAuth integrate as swappable
adapters while users stay first-class Payload documents managed from
the Payload admin. WorkOS and Clerk are deferred post-v1 (SaaS-backed,
not fully validatable locally). Research is done (9-agent workflow,
synthesis `complete:true`); this plan turns decisions D1–D18 plus
payload-onpage precedent into shippable phases.

## Success Criteria

- A site builder installs packages, adds one plugin call, and signs
  in via Better Auth with users/roles/sessions in Payload collections.
- Each provider is an isolated adapter package; core has zero
  framework imports (lint-proven).
- Zero `any` at boundaries; generic-preserving option types;
  canonical `Role` type; `Result`-based errors; Zod boundaries.
- Full e2e: sign-in, callback, logout, admin session
  revoke — green in CI before any release.
- Docs a builder can follow: tour, getting-started, guides, plus
  `llms.txt`/`AGENTS.md` for agent consumers.

## Approach

Clone the proven payload-onpage monorepo shape (core ports,
framework adapters, example app as e2e target, `check` pipeline),
fill it with the auth domain from the synthesis, and ship the two
locally-validatable providers behind `IdentityProviderPort`.
Better Auth first (researched); Auth.js gated on a short research
spike since only Better Auth bodies were inspected. WorkOS and Clerk
stay out of the initial build; the registry reserves their ids.
Re-verify every delegated-research claim against installed `payload`
types and official docs at implementation start; unresolved items
below stay open until then.

## Steps

### Phase 0 — Scaffold and tooling

- Bun monorepo: `packages/{core,plugin,react,next}`,
  `packages/provider-better-auth`, `examples/basic`, `e2e/`.
- TS `strict` + `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` +
  `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` + `verbatimModuleSyntax` + `noUnused*`;
  eslint `no-restricted-imports` boundaries; Prettier; `tsc -b`.
- `check` script: format, lint, typecheck, coverage gates, build,
  size budgets. Changesets, `publint`, `are-the-types-wrong`.
- `examples/basic`: SQLite, self-seeding, reference integration.
- `docs/` skeleton, `AGENTS.md`, `SECURITY.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

### Phase 1 — Core domain and ports

- `ports.ts`: `UserRepository`, `SessionPort`,
  `IdentityProviderPort` + registry, `CookiePort`, `TransactionPort`,
  `LoggerPort`, `TracerPort`, `ClockPort`, `IdPort`.
- Canonical `Role` + smart constructor; typed slug/field map;
  `Result<T,E>` error taxonomy; Zod boundary schemas; startup
  validation (baseURL/secret, default-role-in-roles).
- Explicit composition-root factories. No DI container.
- Unit tests next to code; public API = explicit `index.ts` lists.

### Phase 2 — Payload plugin (first-class citizenship)

- `definePlugin` shape: copy config, append collections/globals,
  merge hooks, chain `onInit`.
- Users collection extension (identities, roles; sessions views and
  admin revoke deferred — not planned for v1, see MISSION.md),
  custom `AuthStrategy` delegating to `SessionPort`, unauthenticated-
  by-default endpoints with CSRF guard + `access.ts`, hook appends,
  RSC admin components (`path#Export`).
- Correctness starters: `pagination:false` on logout finds,
  forward+reverse joins, refresh-disabled session reads,
  configurable query depth. Host-owned migrations only.

### Phase 3 — Better Auth + Next.js adapters

- `provider-better-auth`: `betterAuth({ database: payloadAdapter,
plugins })`, session/cookie delegation, no `next/headers` outside
  the Next adapter, no hand-rolled cookies.
- `@scope/next`: route handlers (`/api/auth/[...all]`), proxy/
  middleware, `nextCookies()` (Edge optimistic + Node full
  validation), `<Provider />`, `useNextRefresh`-style renderer.
- `@scope/react`: sign-in buttons, user menu, admin helpers.
- Integration tests on SQLite-in-memory via `handleEndpoints`;
  security tests that fail without each guard.

### Phase 4 — Auth.js spike, then adapter ✅ DONE

- Spike (`spike.test.ts`, 6/6): Credentials is JWT-only and ignores
  the adapter; credentials + `database` strategy is rejected at
  config time (`UnsupportedStrategy`); the jwt callback re-runs
  without `user` on reads (guard claims); the port reads via Auth's
  own session action (`skipCSRFCheck`, no hand JWT decode).
- `packages/provider-authjs` behind `IdentityProviderPort` +
  registry: engine (fail-fasts, `/api/authjs` basePath,
  claims-callback chaining), Payload database adapter (users,
  accounts, sessions, verification tokens, authenticators), scrypt
  credentials service with builder-stamped verification, port with
  chunk-joining session-id extraction, edge-safe `/cookies` subpath.
- Example coexistence: Auth.js mounted alongside Better Auth
  (`lib/authjs.ts`, `/api/authjs/[...authjs]`, builder-owned
  `/api/authjs-signup`, `/sign-in-authjs` page, concatenated
  middleware cookie names). E2E finding: @auth/core's credentials
  callback always 302s (`json=true` is a v4 convention it ignores) —
  the form follows the redirect and reads success/failure from the
  final URL (`?error=…` on reject).
- Validation: 67 provider tests (unit + SQLite adapter lifecycle +
  error mapping), `bun run check` green, 3 Auth.js e2e specs green.
- WorkOS and Clerk: no spike, no adapter in the initial build
  (deferred post-v1; registry ids reserved).

### Phase 5 — E2E, CI, release hygiene ✅ DONE

- Playwright against `examples/basic` + fresh DB: sign-in,
  callback, logout, admin revoke, role-gated access,
  axe on admin UI. Chromium, CI retries, traces on failure.
  ✅ Local e2e green: 10/10 (Better Auth sign-up/in/out + wrong
  password + role gate + users-admin + smoke + 3 Auth.js specs).
  Remaining: axe pass on admin UI, CI retries/traces already
  configured in `playwright.config.ts`.
- CI matrix: SQLite local, `mongodb-memory-server` replset,
  containerized Postgres parity. Coverage gates enforced.
  ✅ `ci.yml` (check + e2e + release-check jobs, trace artifacts).
  ✅ Postgres: `e2e:postgres` + `dev:e2e-pg`, per-run database,
  13/13 in 11 of 13 runs (two `users-admin` admin-list wait failures;
  structural causes ruled out with DB evidence — no seed dupes,
  no pagination, fresh DB per run — leaving transient slowness;
  spec wait split for diagnosis, CI `retries: 2` covers the
  class). No compose file — GH `services:` in CI, `docker run`
  locally.
  ✅ Mongo: `e2e:mongo` via `e2e/run-mongo.mjs` (per-run
  wiredTiger replset, `transactionOptions: false` in the example's
  mongo branch — three Payload instances lock-fight on one node,
  and our adapters never use multi-doc transactions), 13/13 x3.
  ✅ `ci.yml`: `e2e` (sqlite) + `e2e-postgres` (service) +
  `e2e-mongo` (memory replset) + `check` + `release:check`.
  Note: run parity suites separately, not chained — three
  back-to-back suites saturate one box (mongo leg timed out
  in-chain, 13/13 in 17s solo; CI isolates per job).
- Release checklist: changesets, provenance, no debug output,
  no logged credentials (anti-#154). ✅ Wired: `.changeset/`
  config, `release`/`version-packages` scripts, `release.yml`
  (trusted publishing, provenance), `CONTRIBUTING.md` release
  section. `bun run release:check` (`publint` + `attw --profile
esm-only`) green on all 6 packages as a pre-publish gate
  (kept out of `check` for speed; runs in CI).

### Phase 6 — Builder docs ✅ DONE

- ✅ Tour, getting-started (four-edit drop-in: install, engine,
  config, routes+UI), concepts, Better Auth + Auth.js guides,
  compatibility, troubleshooting, upgrading — all in `docs/`.
- ✅ `docs:api` (typedoc, 0 errors), `llms.txt`/`llms-full.txt`
  (generated by `bun run docs:llms`, drift-proof), media from the
  example app (`bun run docs:media`, 5 screenshots in
  `docs/media/`). Every public API has TSDoc (audit clean).
- ✅ Fresh-eyes validation: independent agent audit of every guide
  snippet against source — 7 factual wrongs found and fixed
  (route import depth, BA model/field constraints, error names,
  measured JWT size, dep classification), plus nits.

## Validation Plan

- Phase 0: `bun run check` green on empty packages; example boots
  and seeds (`bun run dev:example`).
- Phase 1: `vitest run --coverage` passes gates; eslint proves
  core imports no framework; type tests prove generics survive.
- Phase 2: integration suite green on SQLite memory;
  `pagination:false`/join/refresh-disabled behaviors covered;
  admin renders users + identities + sessions.
- Phase 3: Better Auth sign-in/callback/logout pass in
  integration; route-handler + middleware tests green.
- Phase 4: Auth.js integration suite green before merge. ✅
  (67 tests + 3 e2e specs green, `check` green.)
- Phase 5: `bun run e2e` green locally and in CI across DBs;
  highest-risk gate — no release without it. ✅ Local: 16/16 on
  sqlite + postgres + mongo; CI runs all three plus check and
  release-check (first CI run happens on first push — no remote
  yet).
- Phase 6: fresh-clone walkthrough of getting-started by a
  second person (or agent) with zero prior context. ✅ Proxy:
  independent agent audit of all guides vs source; all findings
  fixed and re-verified against source. True fresh-clone still
  wants a human on first publish (no remote yet).

## Known issues, resolved post-Phase 6

- ✅ Auth.js factory-provider bypass: the engine now inspects
  factories the way Auth.js normalizes them (called with `{}`),
  so wrapped credentials fail fast; factories that throw on
  inspection surface `InvalidConfigError` at wiring time.
- ✅ Auth.js giant-claim chunks: `chunkSlots` on the engine input
  (default 3) sizes the session-cookie slots; the middleware names
  mirror it. Only tokens past the raised slots need Auth.js's own
  signout action.
- ✅ Better Auth custom fields + plugin models: `customFields` /
  `customModels` engine options generate matching Payload columns
  and extend the adapter allowlist; strict both directions
  (undeclared extras, declared-but-absent names, and undeclared
  plugin models all throw `UnsupportedSchemaError` at startup).
- ✅ Enterprise review hardening (multi-agent review + fixes):
  open-redirect guard (`safeRedirectPath`, both example forms, e2e);
  logout clears with live cookie attributes (`Secure`/`Domain` via
  `sessionCookieClearOptions`, prefix-derived fallback); server
  authorization helpers (`requireSessionUser`/`requireRoles`,
  example admin page enforced on Node, e2e proves the secret never
  ships to denied callers); credentials dummy-hash anti-oracle;
  `baseUrl`-anchored session reads (host fallback dev-only);
  unified error taxonomy (BA `AdapterOperationError` under
  `AuthLinkError`); Auth.js slug validation parity
  (`resolveSlugs`/`assertUniqueSlugs`, custom-model collision
  checks); shared core guards (`isRecord`/`toDate`,
  `runProviderOperation`, `denyAllAccess`). 331 unit + 17×6 e2e
  green (Next + TanStack × SQLite/Postgres/Mongo; see
  PLAN-TANSTACK.md).
  Proven by `custom-schema.test.ts` (additionalFields round-trip +
  organization/member/invitation CRUD on SQLite memory).
- ⏸️ Postgres `users-admin` intermittence (~2/13 runs): structural
  causes ruled out with container evidence; split-wait added for
  diagnosis; CI `retries: 2` covers. Revisit if it ever fails twice
  in a row or appears on sqlite/mongo.
- ⏸️ Next.js `middleware.ts` → `proxy.ts` rename (Next 16
  deprecation warning, log noise only): staying on `middleware.ts`
  deliberately — `proxy.ts` needs Next 16+ and the peer range is
  `>=15`. Revisit when the floor rises.

## Risks / Open Questions

- ~~Only Better Auth integration bodies inspected; Auth.js needs
  its spike (Phase 4).~~ RESOLVED in Phase 4: spike green, adapter
  - port + engine shipped, session-verify sync proven by e2e.
    (No webhooks in either provider path — sync is read-time via the
    port, not webhook-to-users.) WorkOS/Clerk spikes explicitly out
    of scope.
- Access `Where` shape, full hook arg shapes, `templates/plugin`
  3.x source not inspected — verify against installed types in
  Phase 0/2, not from memory.
- No official Payload testing docs (404) and no published
  `@payloadcms/test` — harness follows onpage precedent
  (SQLite memory + `handleEndpoints` + Playwright on example).
- ~~Postgres parity mechanism (compose vs replset vs testcontainers)
  undecided — spike in Phase 5, default to compose.~~ RESOLVED:
  no compose file — GH `services: postgres:16` in CI, `docker run`
  locally, per-run database names; mongo via in-process
  `mongodb-memory-server` replset (wiredTiger, no transactions).
- payload-auth issue bodies beyond titles and audit-rec landing
  status unconfirmed — re-verify anti-patterns against its `main`
  at Phase 1 start so guardrails track reality.

<!-- docs/PLAN-TANSTACK.md -->

# TanStack Start support plan

## Goal

Make TanStack Start a first-class citizen alongside Next.js: a sibling
framework adapter (`@payload-auth-link/tanstack-start`) built on the
same hexagonal ports, so site builders get identical auth behavior on
either framework with zero provider changes. Day-one target is
Payload v4 (TanStack support ships in `v4.0.0-beta.0`, not v3).

## Success Criteria

- A builder wires Better Auth or Auth.js into a TanStack Start app
  with the same calls as Next: engine, collections, provider
  registration, route mounting, session verification, role
  enforcement.
- The Next and TanStack adapters share one implementation of every
  framework-free behavior (no forked copies).
- A TanStack example app runs both providers with 16/16 e2e green,
  in CI, on SQLite at minimum.
- `bun run check` and `bun run release:check` cover the new
  package; guides document the Start path.

## Approach

Mirror Payload's own adapter pattern: thin framework package over
shared UI. Payload renders one `@payloadcms/ui` behind
`@payloadcms/next` and `@payloadcms/tanstack-start`; we render one
`@payload-auth-link/react` behind `@payload-auth-link/next` and the
new `@payload-auth-link/tanstack-start`.

Four of the seven Next modules are already framework-free
(`handlers`, `verify`, `authz`, `redirect` — pure
Request/Response/Headers/fetch). They move to a new shared
`@payload-auth-link/web` package; `next` re-exports them so existing
imports keep working. Only `middleware`, `client`, and
`server-provider` stay Next-only (`next/server`, `next/navigation`,
`next/headers`). The Start package then holds only Start imports,
per DNA §3 (no framework leak outside the adapter).

Payload constraint: `@payloadcms/tanstack-start` exists only on the
v4 line (beta, no stable). Our plugin peers `payload ^3.0.0` and the
Next example runs 3.90.2, so Phase 0 is a go/no-go compat spike
before any adapter code.

## Capability mapping

| Capability            | Next today                       | Start target                       |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- |
| Mount provider routes | `createRouteHandlers` → GET/POST | Same handlers in `server.handlers` |
| Catch-all API shape   | `[...all]/route.ts`              | `api/auth/$.ts` splat route        |
| Optimistic bounce     | `createAuthMiddleware`           | `createMiddleware().server()`      |
| Server session read   | `createSessionVerifier`          | Shared; headers via `getRequest()` |
| Role enforcement      | `requireRoles`                   | Shared; called from `beforeLoad`   |
| Hydration             | `AuthLinkServerProvider`         | Root `loader` + `initialUser`      |
| Post-auth refresh     | `router.refresh()`               | `router.invalidate()`              |
| Redirect safety       | `safeRedirectPath`               | Shared unchanged                   |
| BA framework plugin   | `nextCookies()`                  | `tanstackStartCookies()`           |

## Steps

### Phase 0 — v4-compat spike ✅ DONE — GO

- Scaffolded `examples/tanstack-start` on `payload@4.0.0-beta.0` +
  `@payloadcms/tanstack-start@4.0.0-beta.0` (file routes per PR
  #16139: `__root.tsx` shell, `_payload` layout, `api.$.ts`).
- Plugin loads under v4 beta with **zero changes**: collections
  register, strategy + endpoints serve, onInit seeds.
- Better Auth signup → session read (JIT user, `roles: [user]`) →
  logout (both providers' cookies expired) verified over HTTP;
  Auth.js mount verified (`/api/authjs/csrf` 200); admin renders.

Findings (all recorded from the spike session):

- **GO.** No plugin rewrite needed; both engines round-trip.
- v4 flips the Local API access default: builder code (seeds,
  scripts) must pass `overrideAccess: true`. Every shipped
  plugin/provider Local API call already does (audited).
- `withPayload` requires the caller to apply `rsc(pluginOptions.rsc)`
  (else SSR 500s); `@vitejs/plugin-rsc` +
  `react-server-dom-webpack` are required dev deps.
- `devServerExternalPackages: ['ajv']` required — ajv's CJS breaks
  under the RSC rewrite (frozen namespace hits `uri.code = ...`).
- Server route handlers receive `{ request }` context, not a bare
  `Request` — shapes the Phase 2 `createServerRouteHandlers` API.
- Spike ran under node; `bun run dev` for this example is untested
  (verify in Phase 3, fall back to node for the e2e webServer).
- `importMap.js` stub suffices for page load; run the real
  `payload generate:importmap` in Phase 3 for admin components.
- Pinned: payload 4.0.0-beta.0, Start 1.168.61, Router 1.170.41,
  vite 8.3.4, react 19.2.6.

### Phase 1 — Extract `@payload-auth-link/web` ✅ DONE

- Moved `handlers`, `verify`, `authz`, `redirect` + tests verbatim
  to the new package; no behavior change.
- `next` re-exports the moved API (back-compat); `next` depends on
  `web`; build refs, typedoc extended (vitest + release-check
  auto-discover).
- Validation: `bun run check` green, 315 unit green,
  `release:check` passes for all 7 packages, Next e2e 16/16 —
  zero regression proven.

### Phase 2 — `@payload-auth-link/tanstack-start` ✅ DONE

- `createServerRouteHandlers(handle)` → `{ GET, POST }` for
  `server.handlers` (uniform error envelope, same as Next).
- `createAuthRequestMiddleware()` — optimistic cookie-presence
  bounce to sign-in via `createMiddleware().server()` (parity
  default; document live-verify as optional hardening).
- Session server functions: `getSessionUser()` via `createServerFn`
  - `getRequest()` headers into the shared verifier
    (`baseUrl`-anchored, CSRF middleware per Start docs).
- `createSessionLoader()` for root-route hydration into
  `AuthLinkProvider initialUser`; `useAuthLinkRefreshStart()`
  (refresh + `router.invalidate()`).
- `beforeLoad` guard recipe using shared `requireRoles` (no new
  authz code).
- Better Auth engine gains a `tanstackStartCookies` plugin option
  mirroring `nextCookies` (verified exported by the installed
  better-auth 1.7.7 `better-auth/tanstack-start` subpath; Auth.js
  needs nothing — `handleRequest` is already Request/Response).
- Unit tests mirror the Next suite (middleware bounce matrix,
  handler envelope, loader hydration, refresh).
- Package re-exports the shared `web` API (same one-import DX as
  `next`).
- Validation: `bun run check` green, 331 unit green (16 new
  - BA engine), `release:check` passes all 8 packages.

### Phase 3 — `examples/tanstack-start` + e2e ✅ DONE

- Example on Payload v4 beta: both providers, sign-in forms,
  account page, server-guarded admin page, Payload admin.
- The 16-spec e2e suite runs unchanged against it (one suite, two
  frameworks — shared `admin-denied` marker, hydration-tolerant
  `gotoOwn`/`toggleToSignUp`, v3/v4 `listTable`/`listCell`
  locators); CI jobs `e2e-tanstack`, `e2e-tanstack-postgres`,
  `e2e-tanstack-mongo`.
- Postgres/Mongo matrix extension done in-phase: 16/16 on all six
  suites (Next + Start × SQLite/Postgres/Mongo).

Findings (all recorded from the Phase 3 session):

- SSR streams before hydration: suite clicks that land in the
  window are silently lost. Both examples render a
  `HydratedMarker` (`html[data-hydrated]`) and the suite waits
  for it (`gotoOwn`).
- `/_serverFn/` must stay public in Start request middleware —
  bouncing RPC corrupts the server-function protocol (redirect
  followed with a JSON Accept → Start 406 → admin detail crash
  on SPA navigation).
- TanStack `redirect()` / `notFound()` must be **thrown** in
  `requireRoles` handlers, not returned.
- v4 admin list renders `grid`/`gridcell` (same `<table>` markup,
  so tbody a11y scoping holds); v4 login adds a show-password
  toggle; v4 ID cells carry an upstream `.id-label` contrast
  failure (triaged exclusion, no-op on v3).
- `bun run dev` verified for the example; no node fallback needed.
- ⏸️ One transient (1/6 runs): post-login SSR to
  `/admin/collections/users` 307-bounced with a valid
  `payload-token` while a later `/me` succeeded — same class as
  the known parallel-worker admin intermittence; CI `retries: 2`
  covers. Revisit if it ever fails twice in a row.

### Phase 4 — Docs + release ✅ DONE

- `docs/guide-tanstack-start.md`, concepts/tour/compatibility
  updates, getting-started + guide-better-auth pointers, PLAN
  counts, llms regen, changesets (minor).
- `release:check` green for all 8 packages; publish together.

## Validation Plan

- Phase 0: scratch app boots, plugin loads, one provider
  round-trip each (manual + recorded findings doc).
- Phase 1: `bun run check`, `bunx vitest run` (315 green),
  `bun run e2e` (16/16, proves zero Next regression).
- Phase 2: new package unit suite green; `bun run release:check`
  covers it.
- Phase 3: TanStack e2e 16/16 on SQLite locally + CI job green
  (plus Postgres/Mongo matrix, done in-phase).
- Highest-risk gate: Phase 0 v4-compat outcome — everything downstream
  depends on the plugin loading under the v4 beta.

## Risks / Open Questions

- **v4 beta churn.** The adapter pins `4.0.0-beta.x`; beta API drift
  may force re-spikes. Mitigation: narrow peer range, Phase 0 records
  exact versions, CI pins lockfile.
- **Should the Next example migrate to v4?** No — stays on v3 until
  v4 stable. Separate work, tracked as a non-goal here.
- **Start middleware runs server-side** (unlike Edge), so full live
  verification is possible there; v1 ships optimistic parity and
  documents the upgrade.
- No Solid/Vue Start flavors in scope.

## Non-goals

- Payload v4 migration of the Next example or existing packages
  beyond what Phase 0 requires.
- TanStack Solid / Vue variants.
- Depending on a future payloadcms.com beta TanStack wiring doc —
  none was found; the PR and demo repo are the wiring reference.

## Sources

- https://github.com/payloadcms/payload/pull/16139
- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/payloadcms/payload-tanstack-demo/HEAD/README.md
- https://registry.npmjs.org/@payloadcms/tanstack-start
- https://registry.npmjs.org/@payloadcms/next/latest
- https://api.github.com/repos/payloadcms/payload/releases?per_page=5
- https://tanstack.com/start/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/server-functions
- https://tanstack.com/start/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/server-routes
- https://tanstack.com/start/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/middleware
- https://tanstack.com/router/latest/docs/framework/react/guide/data-loading
